successors.note: Denmark occupied the duchies in 1712 and sold them to George I of Hanover in 1715; Hanover took de facto possession and paid Sweden 1 million rixdollars under the Treaty of Stockholm (1719). Emperor Charles VI enfeoffed George II in 1733; the Cliopatria Electorate of Hanover starts in 1709.

capitals.name: Stade
capitals.note: Stade was the seat of the Swedish General Government (Generalgouvernement); Bremervörde and Rotenburg were the former capitals of Bremen and Verden. Governor-General Hans Christoffer von Königsmarck held office 1646-1663.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row (its Swedish Empire shapes from 1648 reach 7.4E, so the land is inside them). The page's areas: Duchy of Bremen 5,325 km2 (1803), Principality of Verden 1,360 km2; the circles here total about 8,000 km2 (overlapping), within a factor of 1.3 of the 6,685 km2 and drawn from the prince-archbishopric and prince-bishopric dossiers' circles. The city of Bremen was not part of it.

ledger.note: 15 May 1648: the prince-archbishopric of Bremen is secularised as the hereditary Duchy of Bremen under the Swedish crown. 'In 1648, both prince-bishoprics were secularised' by the Westphalian Peace; infobox 'secularised 15 May 1648'; Stade becomes the seat of the Swedish General Government.

region.text: the Principality of Verden round Verden upon Aller

ledger.note: 15 May 1648: the prince-bishopric of Verden becomes the Swedish Principality of Verden. Verden upon Aller was mediatised by the Peace of Westphalia and incorporated into the duchy; the Westphalia page: Sweden received the prince-bishoprics of Bremen and Verden 'as hereditary fiefs, thus gaining a seat and vote in the Imperial Diet'.

region.text: the city of Bremen and its territory

ledger.note: Early 1653: Swedish troops capture Lehe in the Swedish-Bremen war. 'Swedish troops had captured Lehe in early 1653'; the city of Bremen claimed imperial immediacy to avoid incorporation into the duchy.

region.text: Lehe and Bederkesa, ceded by the city of Bremen in 1654

ledger.note: November 1654: the First Stade Recess cedes Lehe and Bederkesa. 'Bremen agreed to pay tribute and cede Bederkesa and Lehe'; the recess left Bremen's immediacy unresolved (the emperor granted it a seat in the Diet in 1654, a vote in 1663).

ledger.note: November 1654: the First Stade Recess ends the Swedish-Bremen war; the Treaty of Habenhausen of 15 November 1666 ended a second one, with Sweden destroying its fortresses near Bremen.

certainty.note: Drawn as circles round Stade, Stedingen, Wursten and Verden because the gazetteer lacks the Elbe-Weser district names; the page gives areas but no boundary. The border with the city of Bremen is the only one settled by recess (1654) and treaty (1666).

notes: Type colony: the duchies were Swedish hereditary fiefs of the Empire, governed from Stade by a governor-general. Cliopatria's Swedish Empire shapes from 1648 contain the land (bounding box to 7.4E); the renderer should draw it as a tint of Sweden. The eu-08-x batch suggested the slug 'duchy-of-bremen' (1648-1823); the Wikipedia article is 'Bremen-Verden' and the Hanoverian years belong to the electorate-of-hanover dossier, so this one ends in 1719. Four pages opened. Not settled: the city of Bremen's status 1648-1654 (counterpart string 'Bremen (free imperial city)' has no dossier; a free-imperial-city dossier would be a gap-filler), the Land of Wursten (not on the Bremen-Verden page; kept as in the prince-archbishopric dossier), and the 1719 month. Land of Hadeln came in 1731, after this state. The Denmark-Norway dossier files its 1712-1715 occupation under the counterpart swedish-empire.
